name: Drew Ferraro
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember a family paying its school account on a summer morning.” People around Harbour Bakery know Drew by a small Thursday habit. Drew buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I supplied uniforms on credit until her mother's work picked up. I want her to know the debt was paid years ago.
appearance: Drew has a smooth side part with one rebellious curl, two dimples that appear only with a full smile, and a favorite piece of clothing, a striped cotton shirt. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Drew rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Drew is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Drew asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To tell the family the uniform debt was fully settled.
family: Seth Massey is Drew’s first cousin once removed. Drew leaves the first voice message. Seth calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *An ordinary mirror*, Seth says, “I cut a little sample from the replacement glass.”
connections: Benjamin Sun. Wet hair and a school blazer remind two helpers how differently they have known the same child.
